messages:
maria: heads-up — onboarding a new open model 'lark-3b-q4' for structured outputs. Early canary (2k calls) shows lark tends to use single quotes for JSON keys/strings.
maria: parse_fail_rate 2.0% largely due to single quotes and occasional unescaped backslashes.
canary-bot: Canary: /invoke-structured on lark-3b-q4 extra_single_quote_rate=1.6% parse_fail_rate=2.03% (2024-11-10T11:07:02Z).
julia: single quotes are valid in JS object literal but not strict JSON. Could be pretraining style. Are we doing any canonicalizer?
anya: not yet. For other models we added a quote-normalizer but that might mask semantic content.
rod: can we perform a light-weight transform: replace single-quoted keys/strings with double-quoted equivalents only when the outer structure parses after replacement? i.e., attempt replacement and validate.
maria: examples:
```
{'cmd': 'deploy', 'args': {'env': 'staging'}}
{'note': "User said \'thanks\'"}
```
rod: also watch out for escaped quotes inside single-quoted strings. naive replace will break those. Need parser-aware transform.
julia: proposal: run a two-pass postprocessor. 1) try strict parse; 2) if fail, run a forgiving tokenizer that recognizes single-quoted strings and translates to JSON-compliant double quotes carefully (handle escapes), then re-parse. If still fails, flag.
maria: add to canary harness and measure how many are recoverable.
anya: also test quantization: q4 seems to increase single-quote frequency vs fp16 in preliminary spot-check. Maybe tokenizer merges apostrophes into single-quote tokens.
maria: action items:
- @julia implement parser-aware single-quote normalizer and integrate into canary postprocess (due: 3d)
- @rod collect tokenization diffs between fp16 and q4 for a 1k prompt sample (due: EOD)
- @anya gate the normalizer behind a flag and only enable for lark-3b-q4 canary (due: tomorrow)
- @maria expand structured-output testset for lark embedding (due: next week)
canary-bot: Canary job queued for follow-up run with normalizer flag at 2024-11-11T02:00:00Z.
maria: note for docs: mention that some open models prefer single quotes and our SDK will normalize for structured outputs when enabled.
rod: keep an eye for edge-case: `'\n'` sequences that become line breaks if mishandled.
anya: thanks, let's reconvene after the follow-up canary.
